properties.title: SAW: Toward a Surgical Action World Model via Controllable and Scalable Video Generation

membership.reason: SAW is a trajectory- and affordance-conditioned surgical video diffusion world model generating controllable tool-tissue interactions.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L2 action/trajectory-conditioned surgical video world model (WT_PROCEDURE, BP_FORECAST).

properties.backbone: LTX-Video flow-matching Diffusion Transformer fine-tuned with IC-LoRA + depth consistency loss

properties.flow: First frame + action prompt + affordance mask + 2D tool-tip trajectory -> SAW LTX-Video diffusion -> controllable surgical action video

properties.purpose: Controllable surgical action video synthesis for rare-event augmentation and trajectory-driven surgical simulation.

assertions.rationale: Adapts pretrained LTX-Video latent diffusion transformer via IC-LoRA.

Continuous spatiotemporal VAE video latent representation anchored by reference first frame z^f maintains surgical scene appearance and tool-tissue state across the 81-frame generated block (removing first-frame conditioning degrades FVD from 224.28 to 1096.21, Table 2; block-generated future video prediction does not require recurrent cross-call updates).
2D tool-tip trajectory z^p, tissue affordance mask z^gamma, and tool-action text prompt z^a.
Temporally consistent multi-frame surgical video synthesis.
Flow-matching video diffusion transformer with depth consistency regularization.

Future 81-frame surgical videos are explicitly conditioned on 2D tool-tip trajectories z^p, action language prompts z^a, and tissue affordance masks z^gamma; Table 2 ablation confirms removing trajectory conditioning degrades every metric (CD-FVD 199.19 to 344.79, FVD 224.28 to 278.26, PSNR 17.36 to 16.45, SSIM 0.5948 to 0.5818).

Block-generated 81-frame future surgical video prediction is quantitatively evaluated on 542 held-out test clips (Table 1: FVD 224.28, CD-FVD 199.19, SSIM 0.5948, PSNR 17.36, LPIPS 0.4100), outperforming WAN, LTXb, and SurgSora on FVD, CD-FVD, SSIM, and PSNR.
Surgical AI data augmentation and simulator-driven rendering.
Temporal consistency CD-FVD 199.19 vs 546.82 and visual quality on held-out laparoscopic clips.
Downstream action-recognition gains (clipping F1 20.93% -> 43.14%; cutting 0.00% -> 8.33%) on real test data.

evidence_fragments.content: We propose Surgical Action World (SAW) – a step toward surgical action world modeling through video diffusion conditioned on four lightweight signals: language prompts encoding tool-action context, a reference surgical scene, tissue affordance mask, and 2D tool-tip trajectories.
Fig. 1: a) At inference, SAW leverages a user-inputted 2D tool trajectory, language prompt, tissue affordance, and a background surgical scene, enabling realistic and controllable video diffusion.
LTX performs diffusion in latent space using a variational autoencoder (VAE) for spatiotemporal downsampling, with denoising via a diffusion transformer trained using flow-matching [9].

On frame-level content and structural metrics, SAW also outperforms all baselines with an SSIM of 0.5948 and PSNR of 17.36. SAW also demonstrated competitive frame-wise perceptual similarity with a LPIPS of 0.41.
Removing trajectory conditioning significantly impacts performance, as indicated by a consistent decrease in all the evaluation metrics.

Removing first-frame conditioning reduces visual quality, as indicated by drop performance in FVD, LPIPS, and SSIM. Furthermore, temporal consistency is affected as reflected by an increased CD-FVD to 338.75.

In-Context Low Rank Adaptation (IC-LoRA) for surgical action synthesis with four conditioning embeddings: a reference frame zf, language prompt za, tissue affordance map zγ, and temporal tool-tip trajectory zp, enabling the model to generate temporally coherent surgical action videos with realistic tool-tissue interactions (Fig. 1a).
SAW achieves the lowest FVD at 224.28. Moreover, it excels at generating temporally consistent videos, demonstrated through a CD-FVD of 199.19

capability_assessments.rationale: Trajectory- and affordance-conditioned surgical video diffusion world model (LTX-Video + IC-LoRA + depth consistency loss) synthesizing 81-frame controllable tool-tissue interactions, evaluated on 542 held-out laparoscopic clips with trajectory conditioning ablation (L2). Caveat: block-generated video prediction without recursive cross-call rollout, causal identification, or closed-loop policy execution.

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R2 Retrospective laparoscopic video & downstream action recognition

limitations: Offline video generation benchmark; no closed-loop robotic policy execution or clinical deployment.
notes: All 10 physical PDF pages extracted/read; page 3 visually inspected via rendered PNG.

legacy_cells.B: SAW: Toward a Surgical Action World Model via Controllable and Scalable Video Generation
legacy_cells.S: Can conditional video generation produce temporally consistent laparoscopic tool–tissue interaction clips from a reference scene and specified action/trajectory inputs?
legacy_cells.AI: RGB laparoscopic videos; first-frame RGB image; language action prompt; binary tissue-affordance map; 2D tool-tip trajectory maps; depth videos for training depth-consistency loss
legacy_cells.AJ: LTX-Video transformer-based latent diffusion with a spatiotemporal VAE; a cross-attention layer and projection head reconstruct masked depth latents
legacy_cells.AK: LTX-Video (fine-tuned backbone); Depth Anything V2 (generates training depth masks)
legacy_cells.BD: 2D tool-tip (x,y) pixel positions encoded as fixed-radius circles over time; instrument class encoded in the R and G channels
legacy_cells.BN: Depth-consistency loss reconstructs masked depth latents from denoised RGB-video tokens to encourage geometric consistency in the Z-dimension
legacy_cells.BS: Generated 81-frame RGB surgical videos of tool–tissue interaction; training also predicts masked depth-video latent tokens
legacy_cells.BV: LTX flow-matching video-diffusion objective; Smooth L1 depth-consistency loss
legacy_cells.CA: Single NVIDIA A100; fine-tuned for 7,500 steps
legacy_cells.DN: Custom-curated laparoscopic clips sourced from YouTube, HeiChole, Cholec80, SurgVU, and CRCD
legacy_cells.DQ: 12,044 video clips curated from 101 surgical videos
legacy_cells.DZ: Held-out video generation: FVD 224.28; CD-FVD 199.19; SSIM 0.5948; PSNR 17.36; LPIPS 0.4100
legacy_cells.EI: Against WAN, LTXb, and SurgSora: SAW FVD 224.28 and CD-FVD 199.19; SurgSora CD-FVD 546.82, WAN 429.67, LTXb 504.31. Synthetic-video augmentation improved spatiotemporal-CNN F1 for clipping 20.93%→43.14% and cutting 0.00%→8.33% on real test data.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations remove affordance, first-frame, language, or trajectory conditioning and the depth-consistency loss; removing trajectory worsened CD-FVD from 199.19 to 344.79; removing first-frame conditioning worsened FVD to 1096.21 and CD-FVD to 338.75.
legacy_cells.EL: Qualitative examples show generated videos that lack realism or become visually distorted; endoscopic artifacts are noted.
legacy_cells.FB: Procedural scene represented by a reference surgical image and a generated temporal video sequence; SAW performs diffusion over spatiotemporal RGB-video latents, conditioned on tool-action text, tissue affordance, and a 2D tool-tip trajectory.
legacy_cells.FL: Inputs: first-frame RGB, action text, tissue-affordance map, and 2D tool-tip trajectory; frozen spatiotemporal VAE and text encoder form conditioning/video latents; LTX-Video transformer latent-diffusion backbone fine-tuned with IC-LoRA and depth-prediction cross-attention/projection head; outputs generated RGB surgical video and training-only depth latents; no planner.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces a custom-curated laparoscopic video dataset with lightweight spatiotemporal annotations; adapts LTX video diffusion to trajectory-conditioned surgical action synthesis with a depth-consistency loss; demonstrates rare-action augmentation and a qualitative simulator-trajectory-to-video application.
legacy_cells.FN: On held-out video data, SAW reports FVD 224.28, CD-FVD 199.19, SSIM 0.5948, PSNR 17.36, and LPIPS 0.4100. With synthetic augmentation, spatiotemporal-CNN F1 rose from 20.93% to 43.14% for clipping and from 0.00% to 8.33% for cutting on a real test set.
legacy_cells.FO: The simulator-engine demonstration is described as an initial proof of concept; it does not yet enforce instrument joint kinematics or support more instruments and scenes, and inference is not real-time.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work: improve integration of affordance and language cues; generate longer videos; add instruments and anatomical scenes; enforce instrument joint kinematics; achieve real-time inference for closed-loop simulation.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify costly dense annotations or complex structured inference-time intermediates, limited inference-time controllability, and inadequate temporal consistency/realism in prior surgical video generation as motivating gaps.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence supports action-conditioned video synthesis and downstream augmentation, not a validated closed-loop surgical controller or digital twin: the simulator-derived-trajectory demonstration is qualitative and explicitly an initial proof of concept; no real-time, clinical-outcome, or causal-identification evaluation is reported.
